items.title: Library supplement: quadratic feature risks and empirical replacement

source.anchor: Six interfaces: moving features, finite L2 residuals, empirical laws, indexed remainders, Bochner means and true joint data
source.attribution: Samplinglib-authored background development attached by topic to stochastic optimization. These six generic results are not claimed as theorems from the primary lecture notes or as a stochastic convergence theorem.

items.statement: The six complete adjacent statements develop squared-loss calculus from genuine feature derivatives and integrability, identify actual finite empirical risks with L2 norms, derive one-index quadratic replacement budgets, and distinguish arbitrary-law Bochner-mean calculus from finite joint-data scalar integration. All assumptions and endpoint conventions are stated per theorem.
assumptions: Each interface uses exactly its adjacent complete assumptions; they are separate theorems, not one conjunction of all hypotheses.
Squared losses are unhalved; finite empirical probability laws require N>0.
The joint-data theorem uses P and its true input marginal, with explicit actual feature and label L2 membership.

formulae.label: actual indexed empirical budget
formulae.tex: F(\rho^{\rm new})-F(\rho)-\left(\int Vd\rho^{\rm new}-\int Vd\rho\right)=\|f_{\rho^{\rm new}}-f_\rho\|_{L^2(P_X)}^2\le4b^2/N^2.

obligations.label: Differentiate a moving feature and scale the risk
A literal finite-average risk equals its L² norm
Construct the empirical law and evaluate its actual risk
One indexed replacement has an exact quadratic remainder
Integrate the quadratic potential before taking the remainder
A true joint-data risk has a positive empirical replacement budget

assumption_deltas.source: Let H be a real inner-product normed space, with no completeness assumption. Let N be a positive natural number, lambda any real number, phi:R->H, and a,y,v in H. At a real time t assume the genuine derivative of phi is v. Then s↦||(a+phi(s))/N-y||² has derivative (2/N) inner((a+phi(t))/N-y,v) at t. Multiplying that risk by N/lambda gives derivative (2/lambda) times the same inner product. All divisions are real totalized divisions; lambda=0 is an algebraic zero-scaling case, not a temperature model.

assumption_deltas.source: Let P be any measure on a measurable space Omega, N any natural number, a_j:Omega->R for j:Fin N, and y:Omega->R. Suppose every a_j and y belongs to L²(P). Then the actual scalar squared residual (N^{-1} sum_j a_j-y)^2 is integrable, and its integral equals the squared L² norm of N^{-1} sum_j [a_j]-[y], where brackets are the equivalence classes of the stated functions. No probability or finite-measure hypothesis is needed. N=0 uses the empty sum and totalized real inverse.

assumption_deltas.source: Let W be a measurable space with measurable singleton points, Omega a measurable data space and P any measure on Omega. Let N>0, w:Fin N->W, scalar features K:W->Omega->R, and a label y:Omega->R. Suppose K(w_j) and y are in L²(P). Define rho=N^{-1} sum_j Dirac(w_j), using reciprocal N as an ENNReal measure weight. Then rho is a probability measure, the actual loss (integral K(q,omega) drho(q)-y(omega))² is integrable under P, and its integral equals ||N^{-1} sum_j [K(w_j)]-[y]||². Particle values may coincide. No global measurability in q or probability assumption on P is required for this finite atomic assertion.

assumption_deltas.source: Let H be any real inner-product normed space, N>0, a:Fin N->H, i:Fin N, and u,y in H. Let b be any real number and assume ||a_i||<=b and ||u||<=b. Define m=N^{-1} sum_j a_j and mNew=N^{-1} sum_j Function.update(a,i,u)_j. Then ||mNew-y||²-||m-y||²-2 inner(m-y,mNew-m)=||mNew-m||², and this squared remainder is at most4b²/N². The mean displacement is derived, not assumed. No bound on y or the other features, completeness, or measure hypothesis is needed.

assumption_deltas.source: Let W be measurable and H a complete real inner-product space. Let mu and nu be arbitrary measures, feature:W->H Bochner integrable under each, and y in H. Put m=integral feature dmu, n=integral feature dnu and V(q)=2 inner(m-y,feature(q)). Then V is integrable under both measures. With D=integral V dnu-integral V dmu, one has D=2 inner(m-y,n-m), ||n-y||²-||m-y||²-D=||n-m||², and ||m-y||²+D<=||n-y||². The real function t↦||m+t(n-m)-y||² has derivative D at zero. No probability, finite-mass or equal-mass hypothesis is imposed: m and n are unnormalized integrals.

assumption_deltas.source: Let W be measurable with measurable singleton points, X measurable, and P a probability measure on X×R with input marginal PX=P.map fst. Let K:W->X->R. Suppose each K(q) is genuinely in L²(PX), every corresponding L² norm is at most the same b>0, and the true response coordinate z↦z.2 is in L²(P). For any N>0, configuration w:Fin N->W, index i and replacement u, define rho=N^{-1} sum_j Dirac(w_j), rhoNew by replacing only index i, predictor_law(x)=integral K(q,x) dlaw(q), risk(law)=integral(predictor_law(z.1)-z.2)² dP(z), and V(q)=2 integral(predictor_rho(z.1)-z.2)K(q,z.1) dP(z). Put D=integral V drhoNew-integral V drho. Then4b²>0; both empirical laws are probabilities; both actual losses and both finite-law potential integrals are integrable; D=(V(u)-V(w_i))/N; and risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-D equals the input-marginal integral of (predictor_rhoNew-predictor_rho)². This remainder is nonnegative and at most4b²/N². No independence of input and response, global parameter measurability, or assumed pairing/remainder/displacement bound is used.
